While there is no practical failure path today, the two-form match is an unnecessary attack surface.
  Suggested minimal fix: Match only waived_id.strip() and drop the sanitized form from the tuple. An auditor that echoes the raw id (which is what it sees in the prompt for finding_id) will then match naturally because the waiver row stores the raw id as-is.

For finding IDs that never contain formatting characters, these are always identical. The two-entry set is an unnecessary alias mechanism.
  Suggested minimal fix: Build waived_ids from match_finding_id only, which is already the raw stripped id. The finding_id key in the normalized waiver is for prompt display and should not participate in matching.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
Line or code reference: 6551-6558 (waiver_for function, the finding_id alias check)
Problem: The waiver matcher accepts a lossy displayed form of the waived finding_id as an alias. Line 6557 builds a tuple of (waived_id.strip(), " ".join(waived_id.replace("`", "").split())) and accepts a finding whose finding_id matches either element. A waiver for finding_id "SEC`-1" (with backticks) produces displayed form "SEC-1", which then matches a distinct finding whose finding_id is literally "SEC-1" (no backticks) when category, severity and scenario also match.
Why it fails at runtime: A distinct finding with a different raw finding_id is counted as waived and removed from the audit output. This contradicts the PR's stated goal of exact finding_id matching (#6987): the whole point of removing proximity matching was to stop suppressing distinct findings, but the displayed-form alias re-introduces suppression for IDs that differ only in prompt-sanitized characters.

File: scripts/security_audit.sh
Line or code reference: 1787-1793 (matching_waiver function, waived_ids set construction)
Problem: Same alias acceptance on the engine side. waived_ids collects both waiver.get("match_finding_id") (the raw stripped id) and waiver.get("finding_id") (the text_field-sanitized id with backticks removed and whitespace collapsed). A model-reported finding_id that equals the sanitized form but not the raw form of a waived id matches the alias and is suppressed.
Why it fails at runtime: Same as above. Two findings whose raw IDs differ only in backticks or whitespace are treated as the same finding. The auditor prompt tells the model to "reuse its original finding_id", but if the model drops or adds backticks in a later run, a genuinely new finding under the sanitized form of a waived ID is silently dropped.
